dedupe_keys.name: waterproofing data dados a prova d agua citizen science flood and rainfall monitoring app piloted in brazil

description: Waterproofing Data was a research project that built a mobile app, Dados à Prova d'Água, through which citizens record rainfall and local flood impacts and see their reports next to official data, creating a citizen science monitoring network for flood-prone communities. The University of Glasgow's Urban Big Data Centre led it with the University of Warwick, Heidelberg University, Brazil's National Centre for Monitoring and Early Warning of Natural Disasters (Cemaden) and the Getulio Vargas Foundation, and released the app with a school model on 30 March 2022. Coverage is the pilot in Brazil: more than 20 municipalities tested the app, and over 300 students and civil protection professionals in nine cities took part. Format and access: described in a university release republished by PreventionWeb; the project website no longer resolves, so the app's current availability is unknown. Licence: not stated; free to use during the pilot. Caveats: no data set of reports is published, and the evidence is the project's own account. It shows how crowdsourced reports can feed flood early warning and emergency response alongside official networks. A related catalogue record is the Cemaden observation network map.
